sections.h2: What should Scott County, Illinois owners know about property tax?
sections.html:
Scott County has few residents and few staff, so tax questions land on a handful of courthouse desks in Winchester. The county seat sits at 35 East Market Street. Illinois created the county on February 16, 1839, carving it out of Morgan County, and its name comes from Scott County, Kentucky.

The 2020 census counted 4,949 people, which ranks fourth from the bottom among Illinois counties. Census estimators put the July 1, 2025 figure at 4,866, down 4.1% from their base. Some 251 square miles of land work out to about 20 people per square mile, and the Illinois River marks the western edge. Morgan County lies to the east, Greene to the south and Pike to the west.

  • Housing units on the 2025 estimate: 2,377
  • Owner-reported home value, five-year survey ending 2024: $96,400
  • Owners hold 79.0% of occupied homes, and the middle renter pays $689 a month gross
  • Median household income: $66,705
  • Residents past age 65: 26.4%
  • 2023 business base: 84 employer establishments and 604 jobs

sections.h2: Which Scott County offices handle assessments, bills and records?
sections.html:
Three offices cover most property tax questions: the Assessor, the Treasurer and the County Clerk. Each one has its own page at scottcoil.gov and does a separate job in the yearly cycle.

  • The Assessor (Supervisor of Assessments) applies exemptions, maintains the parcel numbering system and the county map files, sends assessment notices, runs the appeal process and certifies the roll to the County Clerk. The office phone listed on the exemptions page is 217-742-5751, and the email is assessor@scottcoil.gov.
  • The Treasurer coordinates collection of real estate and mobile home taxes, keeps the revenue records, disburses the money to taxing bodies and is the contact for parcel questions.
  • The County Clerk joins the Treasurer in running the yearly delinquent tax sale. The county site also lists property records and fee schedule pages for deed and record requests.

The assessor's fee list was updated on April 27, 2026. A property record card costs $1.00, copies are $0.50 per page, a letter-size printed aerial map is $10.00 and an emailed PDF aerial map is $5.00. Pull the record card before a listing, because it shows the characteristics the assessment is based on.

sections.h2: When are Scott County property tax installments due?
sections.html:
The Treasurer posts the payment dates at the top of its page each year, and the 2026 schedule had two parts. Bills were mailed on June 8, then payments came due on July 17 and September 18. Both dates are behind us, so contact the Treasurer for the schedule on the next bill.

Scott County 2026 tax milestones published on county pages
ItemDate
Property tax bills mailedJune 8, 2026
First installment dueJuly 17, 2026
Second installment dueSeptember 18, 2026
Senior freeze applications due at the AssessorJune 8, 2026

Source: Scott County Treasurer and Scott County exemptions page.

Illinois bills a year behind. The DuPage County Treasurer describes the pattern this way: 2025 taxes are billed and collected in 2026. A house sold in autumn therefore still has a bill coming that covers the year the seller owned it. Mobile home taxes pass through the same office on their own bills.

sections.h2: What exemptions cut a Scott County tax bill?
sections.html:
Each exemption shaves the equalized assessed value that the rate is applied to. The county exemptions page lists the programs below, and the Chief County Assessment Office takes applications and renewals.

  • General homestead: covers the rise in assessed value over the 1977 figure, capped at $6,000 in counties outside the Cook County area.
  • Senior citizens assessment freeze: Public Act 104-0452, signed December 12, 2025, lifts the household income ceiling beginning with the 2026 year (payable 2027). Once 2028 is past, the ceiling holds at $79,000 unless lawmakers act again. A federal return with every schedule is the required proof.
  • Returning veterans: $5,000 off for two straight tax years, requested on Form PTAX-341.
  • Persons with disabilities: $2,000 off each year, with yearly verification on Form PTAX-343-R.
  • Standard exemption for veterans with disabilities: $2,500 for a service-connected rating from 30% up to 50%, $5,000 from 50% up to 70%, and full exemption at 70% or above, so long as total value stays under $250,000.
  • Specially adapted housing for a veteran with a disability: as much as $100,000 off assessed value.
  • Homestead improvement: new rooms, remodels and post-disaster rebuilds are shielded for four years, to a limit of $75,000 in fair cash value ($25,000 assessed).

sections.h2: How can a Scott County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
The window is short. Section 16-55(d) of the Property Tax Code gives an owner 30 calendar days from publication of the assessment list to get a written complaint to the Board of Review. A mailed complaint is dated by its postmark, and a courier package by the shipper's label.

The same section tells the board to weigh compulsory sales, including ones the complainant submits, when they share the property's features and condition. Begin with the Assessor's record card and find out what drove the new value. Then collect recent sales of comparable Scott County houses. A losing owner can carry the dispute to the Property Tax Appeal Board. Only the assessed value is in play, since the taxing districts set the rates.

sections.h2: What happens when Scott County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Each year the Treasurer, with help from the County Clerk, sells off delinquent real estate taxes, delinquent mobile home taxes and unpaid special assessments. A parcel left unpaid can end up in that sale.

Call the Treasurer's Office for the balance on the parcel, the sale date and any prior year left open. The County Clerk explains redemption steps and costs, so ask for the balance in writing. Settle any open year before you list, since the buyer's side will run the same search.

sections.h2: How does a closing work in Scott County when tax is still owed?
sections.html:
An unpaid bill does not block a sale, but the buyer will expect it settled by the closing. The closing agent usually gets the balance from the Treasurer, pays it from the seller's share and then records the deed.

  • Section 31-10 of that code sets the state transfer tax at 50 cents per $500 block of stated value, and a transfer declaration (PTAX-203, or MyDec online) goes with the deed.
  • Phone the County Clerk before closing day about recording fees and any county stamp.
  • The 2020 count lists 12.0% of the county's 2,388 housing units as vacant, so a buyer comparing parcels has many options.

Owners who inherited a Scott County house, cannot fund repairs or have fallen behind on taxes have three paths: a listing, a private deal or a sale to someone who takes the house in its present state. That third path skips repair work, and the tax payoff is still settled at closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Scott County, Illinois courthouse?
faqs.a: The county seat is Winchester, and the county website gives the address as 35 East Market Street. The Treasurer, Assessor and County Clerk each have their own page at scottcoil.gov.

faqs.q: What were the 2026 payment dates in Scott County?
faqs.a: Installment one fell on July 17, 2026 and installment two on September 18, 2026, after bills went out June 8. The Treasurer's Office can give the next set of dates.

faqs.q: How much is the Scott County general homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The county page sets the maximum at $6,000 for counties that do not border Cook County, measured against the 1977 equalized assessed value.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for an assessment complaint in Scott County?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days from publication of the assessment list. Put the complaint in writing, send it to the board and keep the postmark or tracking label.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Scott County house if the property tax is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent obtains the balance from the Treasurer and pays it from the seller's share, so the buyer is not left with the debt.
